extracted.intended_audience: researchers, science-watchers, and those interested in scientific integrity, replication, and retractions
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the credibility of published experimental results with attention to replication, data availability, adherence to protocols, and institutional transparency in cases of alleged misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of raw data and research materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the research materials are available to support the findings from the tamarin and chimpanzee experiments. However, there are only summary data, as opposed to raw data, for the rhesus monkey experiments because the researcher ... failed to archive the original field notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw data and research materials should be archived and made available to support reported findings; if raw data are missing, authors should clearly disclose this and, where possible, provide the underlying materials or re-run studies so raw data can be provided (the replication paper reran the rhesus experiments and provided the raw data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct replication of original results
rubrics_metrics.description: The direct replication of the originally reported results on rhesus monkeys in Wood et al. ... found the same pattern of results and is available, including the raw data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A direct replication that reproduces the original pattern of results — ideally with raw data publicly available — strengthens the credibility of an original finding; replications should use the same design and test population where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of blinded coding to prevent bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Each trial was videotaped and coded blind to the experimental condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Video-recording trials and coding outcomes blind to condition reduces observer bias; such blinding should be part of observational and behavioral studies to increase reliability of reported responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to protocols for observing and coding data
rubrics_metrics.description: In one instance of misconduct, he’s accused of bypassing protocols for watching and coding those dull films of one trial after another; as a result, he either saw monkey responses he desperately wanted to see or fabricated responses he didn’t see.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strictly follow pre-specified protocols for watching and coding behavioral data; bypassing procedures is a path to bias or fabrication. Documentation of adherence and oversight is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archiving of original field notes and observational records
rubrics_metrics.description: There are only summary data ... because the researcher who performed the experiments inadvertently failed to archive the original field notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and archive original field notes and observational records so others can verify and audit analyses; failure to archive can undermine trust and impede replication or investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and reporting of more rigorous methods when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: According to the new paper, the authors added 'more rigorous methods' to test the original results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When concerns arise about original methods or data, strengthen methodological rigor (e.g., better controls, blinded coding, full data archiving) and report methodological changes and justifications transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency from institutions about misconduct investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: We’re still waiting, of course, for Harvard to release the report of its investigation into the entire affair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should publicly release the findings of misconduct investigations (or at least clear summaries) to promote accountability and public trust; lack of institutional transparency leaves questions unresolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of retraction in response to confirmed problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Hauser has retracted a 2002 paper in Cognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When errors or misconduct are confirmed, authors and journals should correct the record promptly, including retraction when warranted; retractions are a necessary mechanism to maintain the integrity of the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer independent replication over self-replication for credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The original authors now report that results that they reported in Science are reproducible — by them! Well. Isn’t *that* confidence-inspiring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replications performed by independent groups carry more weight in resolving questions about validity and potential bias than replications conducted by the original authors; disclose who performed the replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific integrity: fabrication is unacceptable regardless of later correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: The point wasn’t whether the original article was right or wrong, the point was whether there was fraud ... Is it somehow more 'okay' to make results up if you find out that you were right, later on?  It is missing the point, which is that it’s not OK to make up data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Falsifying or fabricating data is unethical even if later work or replications happen to support the purported conclusion; integrity of process matters independently of final outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal/procedural requirement for public announcement of ORI conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: If ORI is in fact investigating, and they make a conclusion, then, by Federal Law, they have to make a public announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations by certain federal bodies (e.g., ORI in the U.S.) have statutory requirements for public reporting of findings; awareness of these procedures informs expectations about transparency and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of materials and data to support findings
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the research materials are available to support the findings from the tamarin and chimpanzee experiments ... The direct replication ... including the raw data, is available below, and stored at [link].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make research materials, protocols, and full datasets accessible (e.g., supplemental links or repositories) so that peers can evaluate, reproduce, or reanalyze the work; journals and authors should provide persistent access.
